summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.13/519)

data.turoyo: W marwəxiwo i kalo aʕla w annaqqa, manṭanwo, mfaqṣiwonne w rəqḏiwonne. Rəqḏiwo qumayye.
data.translation: And they would mount the bride on her, and then they would bring them along; they would clap for them and dance for them. They would dance in front of them.

rationale: New II.1 Infectum-wa box; wedding clapping with beneficiary suffix, without inventing a causative dance sense.

summary: New box Preterit: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 1.40/1791)

data.turoyo: ʕƏmri, bele bele, ʕƏsmat Paša kibe tloṯ-arbaʕ (3-4) saʕat kali b Məḏyaḏ, əno ḥzeli, an noše mfaqaṣalle w flan, əno ḥzeli b Məḏyaḏ. E.
data.translation: My age, yes, yes; Ismet Pasha stayed about three or four (3–4) hours in Midyat. I saw him; the people were applauding him and so on. I saw him in Midyat. Yes.

rationale: New II.1 Preterit box, provisionally identified by mfaqaṣ-; retain the contracted target/agent form for review.

summary: New idiom: mfaqaṣle/mfaqəṣ: ḥḏo iḏo lə kqudro mfaqṣo 'eine Hand allein kann nicht klatschen; gemeinsam handeln müssen'

data.headword: mfaqaṣle/mfaqəṣ: ḥḏo iḏo lə kqudro mfaqṣo 'eine Hand allein kann nicht klatschen; gemeinsam handeln müssen'
data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Ḥḏo iḏo, lə koṯe ḥəs mena. Lə kqudro mfaqṣo Ǧan. Kəbʕe d howe “huyoḏo” bayn i ǧamaʕa.
data.translation: Father Brahim: One hand, no sound comes from it. It cannot clap, Jan. There needs to be 'huyoḏo' [unity] among the community.

rationale: New proverb/collocation with one example; iḏo ḥḏo and Ḥḏo iḏo searches had no hits, mfaqṣ found only the inherited wedding example.

summary: Jan Beṯ-Şawoce has no edition translation. English quotations below retain the supplied project machine translation and are marked as such; sense decisions rest on the Turoyo. Where available, round-1 proposals are retained in the human layout and counts, and are not resubmitted in this JSON.
This root has no round-1 job. Original II Infectum remains; Jan adds Infectum-wa and a provisional Preterit. No other stem is inferred.
The one-hand/two-hands comparison expresses communal cooperation but the verb retains physical clapping. Keep one Idiomatic phrases item instead of a new sense or duplicate proverb examples.

The English at 2.4/784 says snapping at, which can misleadingly suggest speech. The Turoyo has the same human-directed clapping/snapping construction as the clear applause contexts; verbal taunting is unproved.
At 1.40/1791 confirm mfaqaṣalle as Preterit and segment actor/recipient; contrast Mfaqəṣalle at 2.4/784, provisionally corrected to Infectum from its ə-vowel.
At 2.4/784 is the gesture applause, derisive clapping or finger snapping? Does it ever lexicalise verbal taunting, independently of hostile speech?
Confirm beneficiary versus patient segmentation of -nne in mfaqṣiwonne and -lan in mfaqṣiwolan.

Clapping can have human beneficiaries/targets (-nne, -lan, -le and l-phrases). The captain’s speech may invoke ironic applause rather than verbal taunting; no separate lexical insult sense is established.
